title: Your Dining Plan Statement: Due Date, Payments, Late Fees, Returned Payments and Disputes
content:
The dining account of a Dining Plan carries the amount the resident owes: plan fees and dining charges add to it, and payments and credits reduce it. A month's charges are gathered on that month's dining statement.

## Statement terms

1. **Due date.** The dining statement for a month falls due on the 1st of the next month.
2. **Payments.** Payments are posted once per payment instrument and applied to the oldest charge first.
3. **Late fee.** A late fee of 20.00 US dollars is charged once per statement month when the statement's past-due amount is at least 50.00 US dollars after 10 calendar days from the due date.
4. **Returned payment.** A returned payment is reinstated - the amount returned unpaid is added back to the dining account - and it carries the returned payment fee of 35.00 US dollars.
5. **Disputes.** A resident may dispute a charge or a redemption only within 60 days after it was posted. The dispute window is counted in calendar days from the posting date, the posting date being day 0, and a dispute raised on the last day is in time. The posting date is the one recorded on the disputed entry of the dining account.
6. **Outcome of an upheld dispute.** An upheld dispute of a redemption restores the credits, referencing that redemption; an upheld dispute of a charge is credited as a charge dispute credit or a billing error credit, referencing that charge. Each entry is credited at most once for each credit reason and restored at most once.

## Late fee threshold on both sides (hypothetical statements)

| Past-due amount after 10 calendar days from the due date | Late fee |
|---|---|
| 50.00 US dollars | 20.00 US dollars, once for that statement month |
| 49.99 US dollars | None |

The fee is charged once per statement month, so a statement month that has already carried its late fee does not carry a second one.

## Dispute window on both sides (hypothetical posting)

A charge posted on 1 March is at day 0 on 1 March, day 30 on 31 March and day 60 on 30 April.

| Dispute raised on | Day count | In time |
|---|---|---|
| 30 April | 60 | Yes - the last day |
| 1 May | 61 | No |

## Points of judgement

- *A payment covers part of the balance:* it is applied to the oldest charge first.
- *A redemption is disputed and upheld:* the credits redeemed are restored once; a second restoration of the same redemption is not made.
- *A charge is disputed and upheld:* it is credited as a charge dispute or a billing error, referencing the charge, and not more than once for the same credit reason.
